title: Default skew tolerance: 30 seconds shipped, floor 5 seconds, ceiling 5 minutes
context: Cloudflare Cron Triggers are documented as scheduling on a best-effort basis; the observed handler start time can drift from the event's scheduledTime. The applied project needs a bounded classification lever so the applied logging companion surfaces cronSkewed for drift the operator cares about and stays quiet within a tolerable window. A per-project fixed default is a starting point the operator elicits away from for tighter or looser needs.
decision: Ship 30 seconds as the elicited default skew tolerance. Enforce a 5-second floor (a sub-5s window flags on normal scheduling jitter and the logging stream fills with cronSkewed noise) and a 300-second (5 minute) ceiling (a longer window turns the signal into an alerting no-op). The elicited answer is written into the applied project as the skewToleranceMs argument on the createDispatcher factory (converted to milliseconds).
consequences: The applied project observes cronSkewed for drift beyond 30 seconds by default; a project needing tighter observability re-elicits closer to the floor; a project running loose crons re-elicits closer to the ceiling. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice (no vendor-documented skew-tolerance default for Cron Triggers; the value is an applied-project observability lever, not a vendor guarantee).
